original_test_intent: Verify the physical USB link from the BMC to the HMC USB hub, the intended hub identity and route, and—per the Procedure—the complete expected downstream population without accepting a generic hub elsewhere in the system.
original_method: Bind the BMC controller/root port through board connectors to the exact HMC hub by stable port path, VID:PID, serial/product and speed; define whether enumeration is observed natively at BMC, HMC or a documented proxy; have an operator inspect/photograph the physical path; collect an unfiltered USB tree and full descriptors plus kernel reset/error history; compare the hub and every required downstream device against an approved manifest; preserve management state and do not unplug, reset, authorize or power-cycle devices automatically.
manual_activity: An operator verifies and photographs the board-level BMC-to-HMC-hub cable/connectors and confirms no service action or device replug is performed during the read-only topology check.
required_inputs: BMC controller/root-port through connector/cable to HMC hub topology and authoritative enumeration surface
Expected hub VID:PID/product/serial/speed/port path and complete required downstream device manifest
Decision whether acceptance is hub detection only or hub plus every downstream device, with missing/unexpected-device policy
Physical inspection, USB reset/error tolerance, management impact limits and recovery
safety_requirements: Use read-only, unfiltered topology and descriptor collection on the approved BMC/HMC surface
Do not match any device merely because its class or text contains `hub`; bind the exact port path and identity
Do not unplug/replug, deauthorize, reset, unbind/rebind, power-cycle or write USB devices without separate approval
Preserve BMC/HMC management and complete USB error history; do not clear logs
Stop on reset storm, device flapping, wrong route, missing management endpoint or BMC/HMC instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate the physical/logical BMC-to-HMC hub map, enumeration owner, hub identity and downstream oracle
After operator path confirmation, capture complete USB tree/descriptors and relevant kernel/management errors
Compare exact hub path, negotiated speed and each required downstream identity with the approved manifest
Do not use insecure/truncated collection, infer a match from generic hub text, alter USB state or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve hub-only Criteria versus all-downstream Procedure acceptance
Approve BMC/HMC controller/root-port/connector/hub identity, enumeration surface and downstream manifest
Review physical, topology, descriptor and stability evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsusb` is appropriate only on the authoritative enumeration surface, but `grep -iE 'hub|usb' | head -n 40` discards topology, descriptors and possibly downstream devices; `sshpass` and disabled host-key checking are unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Collect authenticated, complete `lsusb -t`, full descriptors for the mapped hub and downstream devices, and timestamped USB/kernel errors on the approved BMC/HMC surface, paired with operator physical evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC-to-HMC USB hub path, AI_VR_USB_BMC_to_HMC bundle and 30/30-minute allocation remain; acceptance scope and device identities are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: LOW READ-ONLY BMC-TO-HMC USB HUB TOPOLOGY CHECK WITH OPERATOR CONFIRMATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate physical connectors to an identity-bound USB tree and compare the exact hub plus approved downstream population against a frozen topology manifest.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds controller/port ownership, stable identities, full downstream completeness, speed and error-history evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic hub can be detected while the intended BMC-HMC link is absent or downstream devices are missing; the Master Criteria currently permits that false pass despite broader Procedure coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The path may carry management-critical devices, so even seemingly benign reset/replug or driver rebind actions can disrupt control-plane services.

project_override_considerations: Host-side enumeration is valid only when the platform topology documents that host view as an authoritative proxy for the BMC-to-HMC path. Until Criteria are reconciled, retain both hub-detection and all-downstream evidence without issuing a verdict.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and resolved acceptance scope
BMC controller/root-port/board-connector/HMC-hub map plus operator path photos
Authoritative unfiltered USB tree and complete mapped hub/downstream descriptors with stable identities and speeds
Approved downstream manifest comparison listing every present, missing, unexpected or moved device
Pre/post USB reset/error/flap evidence and stable BMC/HMC management state
Conflict disposition, discrepancy/recovery record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure requires the hub and all downstream devices to be shown, while the Criteria declares PASS when only the hub is detected. These acceptance scopes are not equivalent and can yield different results.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical/topology review can be completed and both scopes documented. The acceptance conflict requires an engineer verdict but does not prevent static review or evidence collection.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2169 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00056-V002: decide whether acceptance is exact HMC hub detection only or exact hub plus all expected downstream devices; approve the BMC controller/root-port/connector-to-HMC-hub map, authoritative enumeration surface, hub/downstream VID:PID/product/serial/path/speed manifest, missing/unexpected policy, physical evidence, error limits, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Exposes the hub-only versus all-downstream Master conflict and prevents a generic or partially populated hub from satisfying the intended BMC-to-HMC topology coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The Procedure explicitly says all downstream devices, but the Criteria says hub detection alone passes. A USB hub can enumerate normally with an empty or incomplete downstream tree, so those statements create a real coverage conflict. Further, a host may contain multiple hubs; a filtered list cannot bind the HMC path. The review therefore requires a port-path and identity oracle plus full downstream comparison, while preserving the conflict for engineer decision rather than silently choosing one scope.
